Even then, Reagan never really listened. If he actually thought cutting taxes for the rich was the cure for all problems, he had a funny way of showing it. His 1981 "tax cuts" were nothing but a mirage for nearly every taxpayer - most of the actual cuts were cancelled out by increased Social Security taxes and bracket creep. He spent the rest of his presidency raising taxes under the guise of "cracking down on IRS enforcement," "raising fees," and "revenue enhancement." He signed off on TEFRA, which was the highest peacetime tax increase in American history at the time. He hiked taxes on gasoline and the trucking industry. He removed several deductions, increasing the burden on high-income taxpayers. Taxes as a percentage of GNP were 18% under Carter and didn't budge from 18% under Reagan. In 1986, federal tax revenues were almost 50% higher than in Carter's last year. This was hardly "trickle-down" in action.

This is nothing new, though. As governor of California, Reagan tripled the income tax during his time in office. California went from 20th to 13th in personal income tax collection per capita and from 4th to 1st in corporate income tax collection per capita. The perception of Reagan as a tax-slasher is unfounded.
